s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion
salient_findings: No improvement with topical corticosteroids and antifungals
Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis
key_facts: Male patient in his early 70s
2-year history of the skin lesion
Lesion located on the proximal portion of the left calf
Mildly pruritic
Erythematous and gradually enlarging
No identifiable cause for the lesion
Topical corticosteroids and antifungals applied for 2 months with no improvement
Physical examination revealed an atrophic appearance
Histopathology showed round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD34 and CD31, negative for D2-40

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion

shortlist.label: angioma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology shows round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: rapidly growing, erythematous lesion with vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation and vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches histopathological features of round vascular channels and endothelial cell positivity for CD34 and CD31

raw.rationale: The patient's age, the location and appearance of the lesion, and the histopathological findings of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma. The immunohistochemistry results showing positivity for CD34 and CD31 also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: angioma
rejected.why: Angioma typically presents as a well-defined, benign vascular lesion, which does not match the ill-defined, atrophic appearance of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Pyogenic granuloma is usually a rapidly growing, bleeding lesion that responds to topical treatments, which is not consistent with the patient's 2-year history and lack of response to topical corticosteroids and antifungals.

rejected.label: bacillary angiomatosis
rejected.why: Bacillary angiomatosis is typically associated with systemic symptoms and a distinct histopathological appearance with bacillary forms, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma is characterized by the presence of hemosiderin deposits, which were not found in this case, and typically has a distinctive targetoid appearance on clinical examination.
